audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted the page's own reasoning and the packet chart. whys[1] calls Level 2 'your first real all-in window' but the row said Skill; whys[3] opens 'It's even' but the row said Kled; whys[4] says 'Genuinely close at 6' but the row said Lillia; whys[6] says 'she out-scales the short-trade pattern late' but the row said Kled.
audit.why: Every one of these rendered a side token that its own why-text argues against, and the packet (Skill/Kled/Kled/Skill/Skill/Kled/Lillia) agrees with the prose on all four.
audit.corrected: Level 2 to Kled, Levels 4-5 to Skill, Level 6 to Skill, 2+ items to Lillia, as matched pairs in both layers; ratings 7/5/5/4. Level 1 left at Lillia rather than following the packet to Skill, because whys[0] says the chip war 'slightly favors her' and inventing a shift there would be dishonest.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blooming Blows was described only as 'her kite + move speed stacks' with no cooldown anywhere, and Swirlseed's timer never appeared.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s — it is up almost constantly, which is why her speed stacks never fully drop. Swirlseed is a flat 12s and is the actual disengage slow. CHAAAARGE is 140s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: The 6s Q, the 12s Swirlseed and the 140s ultimate written into the cooldown block and the phase rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page said Blooming Blows deals true damage on its outer edge, so a reader stacking armour into an AP-looking lane gets no value from it.
audit.why: Riot's Blooming Blows text: magic damage nearby, 'dealing extra true damage on the edge'. Resistances do not answer the edge hit, which is the part that punishes you for standing at trap range.
audit.corrected: True-damage warning added to the interactions row and to itemization, replacing the raw-armour instinct with health.

edits.before: Q beartrap is the kill switch — land it and rip the combo. Only take the trade when Lillia's Blooming Blows is down.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies online — re-E pins her before Blooming Blows has stacked the move speed that kites your dash.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Blooming Blows's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Even: she stacks speed off every Blooming Blows hit, so the re-E only lands if you bait her out and have the Bear Trap slow on.

edits.before: CHAAAARGE turns any side wave into a cross-map gank. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Lillia's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: CHAAAARGE into terrain hard-cancels her kite, but in open lane she just runs your own speed trail — the angle decides it.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Lillia carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Full-AP Lillia W-bounces and E-kites your dismounted form and Lilting Lullaby blanks the all-in. Carry threat 8/10.

edits.before: Track Lillia's Blooming Blows: Her kite + move speed stacks. When it is down — Q-trap + courage all-in.
edits.after: Blooming Blows' outer edge deals true damage — armour won't blunt it, and each hit stacks her move speed.

edits.before: Her kite + move speed stacks. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Every spell hit stacks her speed — engage before she has three.

edits.before: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — Her kite + move speed stacks. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — 6s at rank 1, true damage on the edge, and every hit stacks her speed. - Swirlseed: 12s slow, her disengage. - Your ultimate: 140s, kill windows only.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot vs the poke. Core: Eclipse  (burst + the all-in sustain), then Sterak's Gage; boots Mercury's Treads.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Eclipse, then Sterak's Gage; boots Mercury's Treads. Skip raw armour — her Q edge is true damage.

notes: No mirror existed, so this file defines the chart lillia__kled must invert: Lillia, Kled, Kled, Skill, Skill, Kled, Lillia. I did NOT follow the packet on Level 1 (it wants Skill) because whys[0] states the chip war slightly favours her and there is no evidence for a shift. Deliberately left unstated: whether Lilting Lullaby's sleep is reduced by tenacity or cleansable, and whether Swirlseed's 'terrain' flag means it actually blocks your Jousting dash — Riot's text says only that the seed rolls until it hits a wall, so I made no claim either way.
